searchText: 2 I think? You can imagine one element on the left, one on the right. You'll be able to be able to build a proof for the right side of the tree without the left element *except* for the root node, at which point you need the hash of the left side of the tree, which requires the left element. So the same as a normal merkle tree then. I would expect so, but maybe I'm missing "that one cool trick". 🤷 Was looking at Kate commitments a bit. Looks like you can prove multiple openings in a fixed size proof (hopefully my terminology is close enough to be understandable), but I don't know if you can verify a single opening given such a multi-proof?
